drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: Thank you for your proposal. Attached is a revised discussion draft reflecting the proposed $450,000 Base Salary, twice-Base-Salary severance, and 24 months of continued benefits. We have deleted the non-compete and proposed limited confidentiality and employee non-solicitation provisions, together with cause and good-reason definitions. All revisions remain subject to client approval and agreement on definitive documentation.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of $450,000 (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in employee benefit plans made available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to the applicable plan terms.

3. SEVERANCE. If the Company terminates the Executive’s employment without Cause or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to twice the Executive’s then-current annual Base Salary, without giving effect to any reduction giving rise to Good Reason, in equal payroll installments over 24 months. During that period, the Company shall continue the Executive’s medical, dental, and vision coverage on substantially the same terms as immediately before termination, including the existing allocation of premiums. If continued coverage is unavailable under applicable plans or law, the Company shall provide a taxable payment sufficient to obtain substantially equivalent coverage, subject to applicable law. Accrued salary, vested benefits, and properly incurred unreimbursed business expenses shall be paid separately. “Cause” means conviction of, or a plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty; material fraud or embezzlement against the Company; or willful misconduct or a willful material breach of this Agreement causing material harm to the Company. Cause requires written notice specifying the grounds and, if curable, 30 days to cure. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, a material reduction in Base Salary, a material diminution of duties or authority, relocation of the principal workplace by more than 50 miles, or the Company’s material breach of this Agreement. The Executive must give notice within 90 days after learning of the condition, allow 30 days for cure, and resign within 60 days after the cure period expires if the condition remains uncured. Payment mechanics shall comply with applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code where applicable.

4. CONFIDENTIALITY; LIMITED NON-SOLICITATION. No post-employment non-compete restriction shall apply. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company’s confidential business information except in performing duties for the Company or as permitted by law. Confidential information excludes information publicly available through no breach, lawfully obtained from an unrestricted third-party source, or independently developed without use of Company confidential information. This provision does not restrict general skills and experience, legally protected disclosures, reporting suspected violations to government authorities, or cooperation with investigations, and does not require prior notice or authorization for such activities. Applicable statutory whistleblower protections and trade-secret immunities remain unaffected. For six months following termination, to the extent permitted by applicable law, the Executive shall not directly and specifically solicit for employment any Company employee with whom the Executive worked materially during the preceding twelve months. General advertisements, unsolicited approaches, and hiring without prohibited solicitation are excluded.
